library: LUNAVIA NASA historical visual reference library — Countdown to Launch
purpose: Development references for rebuilding the pre-launch scenes. Not game assets: not in frontend/public, not packaged in the iOS app.

usage_labels.VISUAL REFERENCE ONLY: Study only. Identifiable people and/or NASA insignia: never reproduce in the game or its promotion.
usage_labels.POSSIBLY REUSABLE WITH REVIEW: No identifiable people; NASA content generally not under US copyright, but check credits, marks and endorsement before any direct reuse.
usage_labels.REQUIRES FURTHER RIGHTS CLEARANCE: Not used for any file in this set.

images.historical_context: Launch day, suiting, Manned Spacecraft Operations Building (MSOB), KSC
images.credit: NASA (KSC). ALSJ copy: scan by Kipp Teague; this file is the NASA Image Library original.
images.historical_caption: Apollo 11 Commander Neil Armstrong prepares to put on his helmet with the assistance of a spacesuit technician during suiting operations in the Manned Spacecraft Operations Building (MSOB) prior to the astronauts' departure to Launch Pad 39A. (NASA images.nasa.gov caption.) ALSJ: 'Neil Armstrong and suit tech Troy Stewart during pre-flight suiting.'
study: Clear polycarbonate bubble helmet held in the gloved hands: its red/orange neck-ring seal, the blue and red fittings, the name label 'ARMSTRONG' on the helmet
Neck ring on the suit (red/orange) with the 'Snoopy' communications cap: brown sides, white crown, earcups, twin microphone booms
White knitted comfort gloves worn during suit-up; red and blue wrist rings
Chest gas connectors (blue inlet, red outlet) with yellow covers, white ventilation hose
Technician: white smock and cap, headset with boom mic, cable
Room: white wall panels, grey equipment rack with instruments, white work table
images.rights_notes: Identifiable astronaut (Neil Armstrong, deceased: estate may hold publicity rights) and technician; NASA insignia and US flag on the suit. Do not reproduce in game art or promotion.

images.credit: NASA (KSC). Identities of people other than Armstrong per ALSJ, not the NASA caption.
images.historical_caption: Apollo 11 Commander Neil Armstrong is looking over flight plans while being assisted by a spacesuit technician during suiting operations in the MSOB prior to the astronauts' departure to Launch Pad 39A. (NASA.) ALSJ: Armstrong and Deke Slayton in discussion while suit technician Troy Stewart works on the hoses for Neil's portable cooling unit.
study: Full-height launch suit proportions (standing, unpressurised): folds at the knees, pockets, zipper flap
The white flexible ventilation hoses hanging from the chest connectors to the portable unit
Several technicians in white smocks and caps (one kneeling at the hoses); NASA patch on a smock
Room depth: equipment rack, white table, white wall panels

images.historical_caption: Apollo 11 astronaut Edwin E. Aldrin Jr. is being assisted by a spacesuit technician during suiting operations in the Manned Spacecraft Operations Building prior to the astronauts' departure to Launch Pad 39A. (NASA.)
study: Black pressure glove being locked on: red/orange and blue wrist disconnect rings, the glove's shape and wrinkles
Snoopy cap close-up: brown sides, white crown, chin strap, mic booms
Neck ring in red/orange
Ventilation hoses with yellow covers at the chest connectors
images.rights_notes: Identifiable astronaut (Buzz Aldrin, living) and technician; NASA and Apollo 11 insignia.

images.historical_caption: Apollo 11 Command Module Pilot Michael Collins appears to be explaining a point about his spacesuit glove to technician Joe Schmitt during suiting operations in the MSOB prior to the astronauts' departure to Launch Pad 39A. (NASA.)
study: Black pressure glove (palm, fingers)
Suit test console on the wall: dial gauges, valves, switches, labels
Coiled black communications cord
Technicians' white coats and caps with NASA insignia

images.historical_context: Pad 39A, before launch, Mobile Service Structure (MSS) still nearby
images.credit: NASA. Scan by Kipp Teague (NASA History Office gallery).
images.historical_caption: Apollo 11 Saturn V on launch pad 39A, July 1, 1969. (NASA History Office Apollo 11 Image Gallery.) The ALSJ page lists the same photo as 'S69-38860' in its text but links the file ap11-S69-38660 (typo on that page).
study: Overall rocket-to-tower proportion, side by side with the white Mobile Service Structure
Launch Umbilical Tower painted red-orange, with its service arms reaching across to the vehicle
Hammerhead crane at the top
Mobile launcher base, pad ramp, ground-level vehicles and trailers for scale
Clear-sky sunlight: hard shadows inside the trusses
images.rights_notes: No identifiable people. Saturn V markings ('USA'). Third-party scan credit (Kipp Teague) on a NASA-hosted gallery; confirm before any direct reuse. As a reference: fine.

images.historical_caption: The Apollo 11 Saturn V space vehicle, at Launch Pad 39A, awaits the liftoff scheduled for 9:32 a.m. EDT today. (NASA.)
study: Tower-to-vehicle spacing and service-arm geometry on launch day (arms connected)
The red-orange truss, its bracing pattern, the hammerhead crane
Venting vapour at the stages; morning light
Mobile launcher deck and base structures
images.rights_notes: No identifiable people; 'USA' markings on the vehicle. Factual use without implied endorsement.

images.historical_context: Rollout from the VAB to Pad 39A
images.historical_caption: The 363-foot-high Apollo 11 space vehicle towers over the Spaceport's crawlerway and personnel during its rollout from the Vehicle Assembly Building's high bay 1 to Launch Complex 39A. (NASA.)
study: Scale against the VAB, cars and roads
Tower colour and silhouette from above
Florida landscape and lagoon around LC-39

images.historical_context: Launch day, crew crossing the CM access walkway (Swing Arm 9)
images.credit: NASA (KSC). ALSJ copy: scan by Kipp Teague; this file is the NASA Image Library original.
images.historical_caption: NASA: 'Astronauts Neil A. Armstrong (front) and Edwin E. Aldrin Jr. walk across the mobile launcher to enter their Apollo 11 spacecraft. Along with them is Joe Schmidt, a suit technician.' ALSJ: 'Neil Armstrong and Mike Collins cross the CM access walkway on swing arm No. 9 ... carrying Portable Oxygen Ventilators (POVs) with black hoses. Suit tech Joe Schmidt is behind Collins.' The two captions disagree on the second astronaut; neither is verified here.
study: The walkway as built: an open side with a chain-link mesh fence and a yellow/black striped handrail; a solid side with pipes and fittings
Grated floor, the morning light and haze beyond the open side
Crew in helmets, carrying portable oxygen ventilators by hand (white cases) with hoses to the chest
Spacing: single file, a suit technician following
images.rights_notes: Identifiable astronauts (by context, name tags and caption); NASA insignia.

images.historical_context: A few days before launch, top of the tower
images.historical_caption: A technician can be seen working atop the white room across from the escape tower of the Apollo 11 spacecraft a few days prior to the launch. (NASA MSFC.)
study: The command module under its boost protective cover with the launch escape tower
The tower top: sheds, lamps, girders; a swing arm marked '9' at the left edge
How the white room and the arm meet the vehicle (black and white)
images.rights_notes: People are small and not identifiable.

images.historical_context: Launch morning, high angle from the tower
images.historical_caption: A technician is barely visible performing a last minute task atop the white room next to the Apollo 11 spacecraft a few hours before launch at KSC Launch Complex 39. (NASA MSFC.)
study: The white room as a box at the end of the crew access arm, clamped against the boost cover at the CM
The arm's structure from above, the tower's levels
The ocean and pad perimeter: what the crew would see from the arm

images.lunavia_scene: White room and hatch (end of the walk, boarding)
images.historical_context: Countdown Demonstration Test (CDDT), NOT launch day: crew leaving the spacecraft
images.historical_caption: Within the White Room atop the gantry on Launch Complex 39 Pad A, the Apollo 11 astronauts egress from the Apollo spacecraft after participation in the Countdown Demonstration Test. In the foreground is Buzz Aldrin. Pad leader Guenter Wendt talks with Neil Armstrong. Michael Collins stands to the left of Armstrong. (NASA image article, 25 Jul 2013.)
study: How small and crowded the White Room is: five or six people fill it
Wall-mounted panel with a large round gauge, coiled hoses and umbilicals, white flexible air ducts down the right wall
Fluorescent ceiling light, checklists taped up, red straps
Suit details: neck rings, Snoopy caps, chest connectors
images.rights_notes: Identifiable people; this is a rehearsal (CDDT), not launch-day boarding.

images.lunavia_scene: White room and hatch (end of the walk, boarding)
images.historical_context: Apollo 10 launch day, Pad B: crew already inside, final checks before hatch closing
images.historical_caption: Interior view of the White Room at Pad B, Launch Complex 39, during the Apollo 10 prelaunch countdown. When this picture was taken the Apollo 10 crew had already been inserted into the spacecraft, and final checks were being made prior to closing of the hatch. (NASA.)
study: The hatch opening at floor level: technicians kneel round it and look down into the cabin; a crewman lies on his back in his couch, visible through the hatch
Hatch edge and frame, the hatch door swung aside
White flexible ducting, wall gauge panel, junction boxes with cable connectors, coiled cables, an open checklist on the floor
images.rights_notes: People partly identifiable; NASA insignia. Different mission and pad: architecture only.

images.lunavia_scene: White room and hatch (end of the walk, boarding)
images.historical_context: Apollo 9 Countdown Demonstration Test, Pad A (rehearsal)
images.historical_caption: Interior view of the white room atop Pad A, Launch Complex 39, during Apollo 9 Countdown Demonstration Test activity. Standing next to spacecraft hatch is astronaut James A. McDivitt, commander. (NASA.)
study: The same room as Apollo 11 (Pad A) with the hatch open: hatch door, its mechanism, the cabin beyond
Helmets and gloves being handled; technicians' white coveralls, caps, a hard hat, headsets
Floor colour (blue-grey), white walls, ducting
images.rights_notes: Identifiable astronaut; rehearsal on a different mission.

images.credit: NASA History Office, Apollo diagrams collection
images.historical_caption: Command Module Interior, from Apollo Training Manual 'Apollo Spacecraft & Systems Familiarization' (March 13, 1968). Left- and right-side cutaways with labels.
study: Layout of the equipment bays round the couches
Where the pressure suit connectors, ECS panels, guidance computer, optics and stowage sit
The couch frame and its struts (left side view)
images.rights_notes: US Government technical drawing, no people; check any contractor marks before direct reuse.

images.historical_caption: Command Module Interior, from Apollo Training Manual 'Apollo Spacecraft & Systems Familiarization' (March 13, 1968). Sheet titled 'Apollo CM Interior Configuration: LHEB, LHFEB, UEB & Left AB', view looking down and outboard.
study: Equipment-bay panels, lockers and doors with their latches
Instrument density on the bay panels
The rounded cone wall and the frames that structure it

images.credit: NASA History Office, Apollo diagrams collection
images.historical_caption: Command Module Main Control Panel, from Apollo Operations Handbook Block II Spacecraft (October 15, 1969). Sectional scans (ad019a–f) are linked from the same page.
study: The main display console as ONE continuous wing-shaped panel spanning all three couches
The two attitude balls (FDAI), the DSKY, the caution-and-warning matrix, gauges, hundreds of toggle switches
Panel grouping and spacing for texture work
